main_text.p: turgiam & confecrationem La-tine peragendam, vel Sacramen-tum Cœnæ in proprie dictum Sacrificium permutandum. Id quod & jam, & deinceps, pro vi-rili, defendere sumus parati. Hi carceres nostræ metæ sunto, hi limites, quos extra currere volu-pe non est. Sive igitur sudantes jam, madentésque chartæ no-stræ torqueantur, sive deinceps contradictionis fatum sint ex-perturæ, id unum τὰς ἀντιλέγοντας[?] ro-gamus, ut ne ad Andabatarum, inutilem pariter atque inglo-riam, nos provocent pugnam: Non ingenii hic lusus, non sci-entiæ tantum exercitium; con-scientiæ etiam sacrum certamen est & examen, utrum cibum, ve-

page.notes: The Greek words after "unum" are printed small and raised; the reading τὰς ἀντιλέγοντας is uncertain, and the final letters are doubtful. The catchword "re" is at the lower right. The first word "turgiam" is a line fragment at the top of the page and is kept as printed.
